newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak central bank says no repo tender on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Slovak central bank says no repo tender on Monday.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold a tender for short-term securities repurchase on Monday.
According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector is short of liquidity, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 92.28 percent as of Friday.

The NBS holds tenders on a daily basis, if needed, instead of quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates. The move is the latest effort by the NBS to rein in a rapidly growing money supply and cool off a consumption-led boom.
The key money measure, M2, rose 19.0 percent year-on-year in November, compared with a 17.9 percent increase in October, the NBS said.
